title: Best dairy-free protein sources: animal and plant options

seo.title: Best dairy-free protein sources and how much they provide
seo.meta_description: Chicken, fish, eggs, tofu, tempeh, seitan and beans all provide protein without dairy. Compare grams per 100 g and realistic servings.
seo.search_intent: Find high-protein foods that contain no dairy, including both animal and plant options with comparable serving amounts.

excerpt: Avoiding milk, yogurt, and cheese does not require specialty protein products. Cooked chicken breast can provide about 30 grams protein per 100 grams, firm tofu roughly 15–18 grams, cooked lentils 9 grams, and one large egg about 6 grams.
content_html:
A dairy-free diet can still be extremely protein-rich using ordinary foods. The main rule for comparing them is to avoid mixing dry powders, raw ingredients, and cooked foods in one ranking. Ready-to-eat values produce a much more honest comparison.

Protein-dense dairy-free choices

Ready-to-eat foodApprox. protein per 100 gPractical serving example
Cooked skinless chicken breast~30–31 g5 oz: ~43–44 g
Canned tuna in water, drained~25–27 g3 oz: ~21–23 g
Prepared seitan~20–30 g4 oz: ~23–34 g
Cooked salmon~20–23 g5 oz: ~28–33 g
Tempeh~19–20 g4 oz: ~22 g
Firm tofu~15–18 g5 oz: ~21–26 g
Hard-boiled egg~12.6 g1 large: ~6.3 g
Cooked lentils~9 g1 cup: ~18 g
Cooked chickpeas~8.9 g1 cup: ~14–15 g

Meat and fish pack a lot of protein into a small volume

Chicken, turkey, fish, and canned seafood commonly provide roughly 20–31 g protein per 100 g cooked or drained. A 5-ounce chicken serving can exceed 40 g protein, while 5 ounces of salmon typically provides around 28–33 g.

The rest of the nutrition profile still matters: salmon contains substantially more fat than skinless breast but also provides EPA and DHA.

Eggs provide a convenient fixed portion

Hard-boiled egg is about 12.6 g protein/100 g. One large egg provides around 6–6.5 g, so two eggs contribute roughly 12–13 g protein.

Eggs also supply choline, vitamin B12, selenium, and other nutrients, so protein concentration is not the only useful metric.

Soy foods are especially useful plant options

Tempeh is around 19–20 g protein/100 g. Firm tofu often provides roughly 15–18 g depending on water content. A 5-ounce portion of firm tofu can therefore provide about 21–26 g protein.

Seitan is concentrated but not gluten-free

Prepared seitan often provides 20–30 g protein/100 g. Because it is made primarily from wheat gluten, it is not suitable for celiac disease. Commercial versions can also be high in sodium.

Beans trade some protein density for fiber

Cooked lentils and chickpeas provide about 9 g protein/100 g. One cooked cup of lentils is close to 18 g protein. That is much less protein than the same weight of chicken, but lentils also provide roughly 15–16 g fiber per cup while meat and fish provide zero fiber.

Nuts and seeds are useful supplements, not always the most efficient protein centerpiece

Some nuts and seeds exceed 20 g protein/100 g, but a usual serving is around 1 ounce, not 100 g. One ounce of almonds is about 6 g protein and roughly 164 calories. They can add protein, but reaching 30–40 g primarily through nuts also adds substantial energy.

Dairy-free is not the same as vegan

Eggs, meat, and fish are dairy-free because dairy specifically refers to milk-based foods. If the diet is also vegan, the relevant options are tofu, tempeh, seitan if gluten is tolerated, legumes, nuts, seeds, and other plant foods.

The useful takeaway

For a high amount of dairy-free protein in a modest serving, chicken, seafood, seitan, tempeh, and firm tofu stand out. Eggs and legumes are less concentrated but bring other useful nutrients. The best choice depends on whether dairy-free also means vegetarian, vegan, lower-fat, or higher-fiber for you.

faq.question: What dairy-free food is highest in protein?
faq.answer: Cooked chicken breast is around 30–31 g/100 g, drained tuna roughly 25–27 g, and many prepared seitan products 20–30 g. Tempeh and firm tofu are strong plant options.

faq.question: Are eggs dairy?
faq.answer: No. Eggs are animal foods, but dairy specifically comes from milk.

faq.question: What high-protein options are both dairy-free and vegan?
faq.answer: Tofu, tempeh, seitan if you tolerate gluten, lentils, chickpeas, other legumes, nuts, and seeds.
